findings.claim: MessagePack attributes on T are ignored unless the user separately creates a surrogate. When no surrogate is supplied, the collector always builds contractless name-keyed members, without checking for [MessagePackObject]/[Key]/[IgnoreMember]. This violates the acceptance criterion that MessagePack attributes on T be honoured: an attributed external type would serialize as a contractless map rather than using its declared keys and membership.

receipt_plan.detail: Add an execution test for an external T marked [MessagePackObject], with [Key(0)] on one member and [IgnoreMember] on another, and a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] without SurrogateType. Serialize T and assert a one-element integer-keyed array containing only the keyed member; the current implementation instead produces a contractless string-keyed map.

findings.claim: The new attribute deliberately creates an explicit opt-in exception to the usual rule that metadata-only types are not analyzed or given formatters by the consuming assembly; the existing default behavior remains unchanged.

receipt_plan.detail: [L11] records that referenced-assembly types ordinarily receive no analysis or formatter and that this is deliberate. Here generation occurs only for a consumer-declared class explicitly annotated with [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter], as required by REQ-2129, rather than for all metadata-only types.
